item.title: Israel and Hezbollah continue to trade blows despite the ceasefire
item.description: Israel has taken responsibility for Wednesday night's strike on the southern suburbs of Beirut, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu saying he personally authorised the attack to kill a top Hezbollah Commander identified as Malek Balou. The continued ceasefire incursions are further pressuring talks between Tel Aviv and Beirut, which are being supported by the US. item.title: Middle East war back on? UAE responds to fresh attacks, US and Iran trade fire
item.description: The United Arab Emirates says it's responded to fresh missile and drone attacks by Iran this Friday. The strikes come hours after the US says three of its navy destroyers in the Strait of Hormuz were targeted. President Donald Trump ordered retaliatory strikes - but then downplayed the hostilities and said the ceasefire still stands. Analysis by Douglas Herbert, FRANCE 24 international affairs commentator.

item.title: What you need to know about the 7 May elections in England, Scotland and Wales
item.description: Millions will vote in parliamentary elections in Scotland and Wales, and local elections in England.

item.title: Iran on the verge of economic asphyxiation -- rare footage from Tehran
item.description: Two months ago, Donald Trump claimed the United States would liberate the Iranian people when it launched the offensive alongside Israel. Two months into the war, the regime is still there, the repression continues, and the country stands on the verge of economic asphyxiation. Our colleagues at France 2 had the rare opportunity to film the lives of Iranians in the heart of Tehran, where runaway inflation has led to a cost of living crisis.

item.title: US military says it intercepted Iranian attacks in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: On Thursday, the US and Iran exchanged accusations and fire in the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington saying it intercepted Iranian attacks and struck back at military targets, while Tehran reported retaliatory action and rising regional tensions. The fragile ceasefire faced fresh strain amid widening conflict risks.

item.title: U.S. strikes two Iranian-flagged vessels as tensions continue amid ceasefire
item.description: The Trump administration, sidestepping a widening battle in the Strait of Hormuz, said it was anticipating a reply from Tehran on its latest terms for ending the war.

item.title: U.S. intercepts Iranian attacks on 3 ships. And, what to know about hantavirus
item.description: The U.S. says it intercepted Iranian attacks yesterday targeting three Navy ships. And, what to know about the hantavirus outbreak that started on a cruise ship.

item.title: Iran and the US trade fire over Hormuz, Trump says ceasefire still in effect
item.description: A new exchange of fire between Iran and the US occurred late Thursday night in the Strait of Hormuz, with both countries accusing each other of firing first. The latest by Simon Moritz.

item.title: Sporadic clashes erupt between ‌Iranian and US forces ‌in Hormuz strait
item.description: Sporadic clashes erupted between Iranian and US forces on Friday in the Strait of Hormuz after the US fired at two empty oil tankers trying to break the blockade by heading for an empty Iranian port in the Gulf of Oman, the American military said. Late on Friday, the US and Iran also traded fire in the first real challenge to the fragile ceasefire. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz: What role for France?
item.description: Europe's most powerful warship is inching closer to the strategic waterway whose effective closure has come to epitomise the war in Iran. France is moving its aircraft carrier group towards the Strait of Hormuz, as it works with the UK on a proposal that aims ​to lay the groundwork for safe transit through the Strait once the conflict is resolved.
